findings.checklist_item: - [ ] If the hop-limit contingency fires, the ADR 0046 entry must explicitly state that the change grants all shared-bridge containers (including the publicly-reachable Gerrit container) direct live IMDS access for fresh STS credentials — not merely the same access level as the pre-materialized .env — and record this as the accepted, bounded exposure with its specific blast-radius rationale.

ABSENCE: The contingency rationale does not distinguish between static .env credential access (current) and live on-demand IMDS STS credential fetch (contingency path adds), which differ in freshness and revocability window.
findings.finding: The contingency-path rationale elides a qualitative credential-access distinction: in the hop-limit=2 path, all containers including Gerrit (publicly reachable via port 29418/tcp open to 0.0.0.0/0) gain live IMDS access and can obtain fresh short-lived STS credentials on demand — not merely the static pre-materialized .env secrets they already share. The plan body argues the containers are 'already inside the same trust boundary' because they share .env secrets, but this underdeclares the contingency's actual posture change; the ADR 0046 entry the plan commits to writing (AC7) should explicitly acknowledge this distinction.
findings.location: Approach section — contingency rationale paragraph; AC7 (contingency ADR 0046 entry)
scenarios: An RCE exploit in Gerrit (reachable via public SSH port 29418) allows an attacker to pivot to IMDS and obtain fresh instance-role credentials on demand — credentials that now include bedrock:InvokeModel — rather than being limited to the static .env values that were materialized at last boot.
The ADR 0046 exception entry, as currently planned, may record only that hop-limit was raised without capturing this specific escalation in the blast radius.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the ADR 0046 exception template in the plan: 'Notably, this also grants the Gerrit container (which accepts inbound connections on public port 29418) live IMDS credential fetch capability; a container-level compromise would therefore yield on-demand short-lived STS credentials rather than only the boot-time-materialized .env values. This is accepted because [the instance role's Bedrock grant is now present regardless / the blast radius remains confined to this single-tenant host / rotation is possible via instance-profile replacement]; the deferred hardening path is named-network isolation (tracked separately).' Ensure this text appears in the actual ADR 0046 amendment, not just the plan document.

evidence: `pydantic_ai.models.bedrock.BedrockConverseModel` EXISTS in the installed environment (resolved via symbol lookup)

The verification test uses 'bedrock-runtime Converse call' via raw boto3 — this call goes through bedrock:Converse at the IAM layer, NOT bedrock:InvokeModel, yet the plan lists only InvokeModel in the grant
findings.finding: The plan grants `bedrock:InvokeModel` and `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` in `iam_s7.tf`, but pydantic-ai's Bedrock integration (`pydantic_ai.models.bedrock.BedrockConverseModel`, confirmed installed) uses the Bedrock **Converse API** (`bedrock:Converse` / `bedrock:ConverseStream`), not the InvokeModel API. The verification test (raw boto3 `bedrock-runtime` Converse call) also uses the Converse API but exercises it via direct boto3, which may succeed regardless — masking the mismatch. When S8 routes through `PydanticAIRunner` → `BedrockConverseModel`, the container will receive `AccessDeniedException` on `bedrock:Converse` because that action was never granted in S7.
findings.location: Approach section — IAM grant: 'bedrock:InvokeModel + bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream'; Testing section — 'a minimal bedrock-runtime Converse call'
scenarios: S8 lands, sets REBAR_LLM_MODEL to a Bedrock model string, PydanticAIRunner builds a BedrockConverseModel, which calls bedrock:Converse — the container gets AccessDeniedException because S7 only granted InvokeModel.

The S7 verification test (raw boto3 Converse) passes because the boto3 Converse call goes to bedrock:Converse, which is separately available to the role via other means or the test is misconfigured — either way the IAM action mismatch is not caught.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the two InvokeModel actions with `bedrock:Converse` and `bedrock:ConverseStream` (or include all four if both raw and pydantic-ai paths need to be supported). Confirm by inspecting `pydantic_ai/models/bedrock.py` for the boto3 method calls it makes (`client.converse` → `bedrock:Converse`; `client.converse_stream` → `bedrock:ConverseStream`).

findings.finding: The plan names `infra/terraform/iam.tf` as the edit target for the new Bedrock IAM policy statement, but iam.tf's own SINGLE-OWNER CONTRACT comment (lines 4-9) explicitly states: 'Downstream stories MUST NOT create another role — they ATTACH their own separately-named, scoped inline policies to this same role.' The established pattern is a separate `iam_s<N>.tf` file (see iam_s2.tf, iam_s4a.tf), not a direct edit to iam.tf. Naming iam.tf as the edit target conflicts with the contract this story itself operates under.

findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'infra/terraform/iam.tf — the scoped Bedrock statement on rebar-gerrit-instance-role' with 'infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf (new file) — the scoped Bedrock inline policy attached to rebar-gerrit-instance-role, following the iam_s2.tf / iam_s4a.tf pattern; iam.tf is NOT edited directly (per SINGLE-OWNER CONTRACT).'

findings.finding: The plan's Scope section directs edits to S1-owned `infra/terraform/iam.tf` directly, but `iam.tf` carries an explicit single-owner contract (lines 4–9) stating that downstream stories must attach 'separately-named, scoped inline policies' via their own `iam_sN.tf` files — exactly the pattern `iam_s2.tf` and `iam_s4a.tf` follow. Writing a new `aws_iam_role_policy` resource into `iam.tf` from S7 violates that contract, makes the S1-owned file a multi-story accumulation point, and risks future apply conflicts if S1 is ever re-applied or refactored independently.
findings.location: Scope section ('infra/terraform/iam.tf — the scoped Bedrock statement'); infra/terraform/iam.tf lines 4–9

findings.finding: The plan's mechanism is incomplete: adding a Bedrock IAM policy to the instance role does not cause the review-bot to call Bedrock. The review-bot currently uses the Anthropic SDK via `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (fetched from SSM by `fetch-secrets.sh`, injected via `env_file: .env` in `docker-compose.yml`, consumed by `pydantic-ai`'s `AnthropicProvider`). An IAM `bedrock:InvokeModel` grant on the instance role is inert unless the application is also directed to use a Bedrock endpoint — e.g., by switching `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` to a `bedrock:`-qualified model string, installing the appropriate pydantic-ai Bedrock provider, providing `AWS_REGION` in the review-bot container environment, and either removing or conditionalising `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. None of this application-layer wiring is specified.
findings.location: Approach section / Scope section; `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh:81,116`; `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:86-88` (`env_file: .env`); `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py`

findings.finding: The plan grants bedrock:InvokeModel + bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream and validates with a boto3 bedrock-runtime Converse call (AC3), but the review-bot's actual LLM runtime has no Bedrock code path: pydantic-ai uses AsyncAnthropic talking directly to api.anthropic.com via ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The _PAI_PROVIDER_PREFIX map in src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py has no 'bedrock' entry; the voter.py boto3 calls are best-effort CloudWatch metric publishes, not inference. The plan never specifies what code change (new model_provider, new provider prefix, different SDK) would cause the review-bot to actually consume Bedrock credentials — leaving the IAM grant potentially unused by the running software.
findings.location: Approach section (IAM grant + alternative rejection) and AC3 ('a bedrock-runtime Converse call … returns 200')

findings.finding: The plan adds `bedrock:InvokeModel`/`bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` IAM permissions and AC #2 asserts 'a Bedrock Converse call from inside the review-bot container succeeds using instance-role credentials' — but the review-bot's LLM stack currently routes exclusively through the direct Anthropic API (AsyncAnthropic client to api.anthropic.com, keyed by ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). No client-code change is specified to redirect calls to the AWS Bedrock endpoint. The IAM permission is necessary but not sufficient: the code must also be changed to use `AnthropicBedrock` (anthropic SDK) or `BedrockProvider` (pydantic-ai, which EXISTS in the installed environment) instead of the current `AsyncAnthropic`/`AnthropicProvider` path, and `fetch-secrets.sh` still fetches `anthropic-api-key` from SSM into the container env. Without this code-path change, the IAM grant changes nothing about how the container authenticates to Claude.
findings.location: Approach section ('a minimal bedrock-runtime Converse call'); AC #2; infra/terraform/iam.tf (proposed Bedrock statement); src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py; src/rebar/llm/runner.py
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Scope: 'src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py (or runner.py) — add a Bedrock provider path using pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock.BedrockProvider (already in the installed environment) when REBAR_LLM_USE_BEDROCK=1 or when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is absent and AWS_REGION is set, so instance-role credentials are used via boto3.' Also update fetch-secrets.sh scope to clarify whether ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is removed from the container env or coexists.

findings.finding: The bot's LLM client stack (src/rebar/llm/) exclusively uses the Anthropic direct SDK (AsyncAnthropic / AnthropicProvider) with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY sourced from SSM, not boto3 bedrock-runtime. Granting Bedrock IAM permissions and raising the IMDS hop limit will not cause the bot to call Bedrock — the code must be re-wired to a boto3 bedrock-runtime client (or a Bedrock-backed pydantic-ai provider) for instance-role credentials to be used. That code change is absent from the plan's Scope section, yet the Testing and AC sections assert a 'Bedrock Converse call from inside the review-bot container succeeds using instance-role credentials'. The integration as described cannot be achieved without first modifying the LLM client.
findings.location: Scope section (no src/rebar/llm/ change listed); Testing happy path; AC line 2 ('a Bedrock Converse call from inside the review-bot container succeeds using instance-role credentials')
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) add a Scope item for adding a boto3 bedrock-runtime call path to rebar.llm (e.g. a `bedrock` provider in `anthropic_model.py` or a new `bedrock_model.py` module) and update fetch-secrets.sh to omit ANTHROPIC_API_KEY once the bot uses the instance role, or (b) if Bedrock is only for one use-case (e.g. the opcert gate), scope and name that consumer explicitly and add its code change.
